- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — adjust downward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >80) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish — add 1–3% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently low (below 0.4), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–4 days — apply a 1–2 day lead correction for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
- Mean reversion occurs after 10–15 day spikes — reduce forecast slope after 10-day high to align with historical 30-day mean.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is rising steadily, forecast should be slightly higher than 30-day moving average — use sentiment as a multiplier (0.95–1.05) for price adjustment.
